حِنْدِسٌ Darkness: (K:) or intense darkness: (Ham p. 140:) pl. حَنَادِسُ. (K.) You say, سَرَوْا فِى حِنْدِسِ اللَّيْلِ [They journeyed in the darkness, or intense darkness, of the night]: and فِى حَنَادِسِ الظُّلَمِ [in the darkness, or intense darkness, of the nights called الظُّلَم, q. v.]. (A, in art. حدس.) Z derives it from الحَدْسُ meaning نَظَرٌ خَافٍ. (TA. [See art. حدس.]) ―
-b2- Also, as an epithet applied to night, (S, K,) Dark: (K:) or intensely dark; (S;) and so ↓ مُحَنْدِسٌ . (Ham p. 140.) You say لَيْلٌ حِنْدِسٌ and لَيْلَةٌ حِنْدِسَةٌ. (TA.) ―
-b3- [Hence,] الحَنَادِسُ Three nights (K, TA) of the lunar month, (TA,) next after the
ظُلَم [q. v.]. (K.) ―
-b4- [Hence also,] أَسْوَدُ حِنْدِسٌ, a phrase like أَسْوَدُ حَالِكٌ [Intensely black]. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
